title: Charlson Comorbidity Index
keywords: 1 point conditions include MI CHF PVD CVA dementia COPD
2 point conditions include hemiplegia moderate-severe CKD diabetes with end-organ damage any tumor leukemia lymphoma
6 points metastatic solid tumor or AIDS
age adjustment adds a point per decade over 40 up to 4
sources: Charlson ME, Pompei P, Ales KL, MacKenzie CR. A new method of classifying prognostic comorbidity in longitudinal studies: development and validation. J Chronic Dis. 1987;40(5):373-383.
Point values and age-adjustment structure WebSearch-verified against the original 1987 derivation.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 4). Built as an age-adjusted score (age contributes points directly, per the standard age-adjusted CCI variant) rather than a separate age-multiplier step, since that's how it's most commonly used at the bedside.

purpose: Quantify overall comorbidity burden for prognosis, risk adjustment, and framing long-term outcome conversations — widely used in research and increasingly at the bedside for perioperative and critical-care risk discussions.
notes: This is a general comorbidity-BURDEN score, not a replacement for a disease-specific severity score (APACHE II, SOFA, etc.) in the acutely ill patient — it reflects chronic health going INTO an illness, not how sick the patient is right now. Count only conditions that are present/active or a permanent sequela (e.g. prior stroke with residual deficit counts; a fully resolved, one-time event generally does not) — use clinical judgment on borderline cases, this tool doesn't adjudicate them for you.

items.label: Number of 1-point conditions present (myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, cerebrovascular disease/TIA, dementia, chronic pulmonary disease, connective tissue disease, peptic ulcer disease, mild liver disease, diabetes without end-organ damage — 10 possible) — count how many apply

Number of 2-point conditions present (hemiplegia/paraplegia, moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease, diabetes WITH end-organ damage, any non-metastatic solid tumor, leukemia, lymphoma — 6 possible) — count how many apply

interpretation.label: Score 0
interpretation.detail: Approximate 1-year mortality ~ 12% in the original cohort — lowest comorbidity burden band. Treat as an order-of-magnitude estimate; absolute mortality figures from a 1987 derivation cohort don't transfer precisely to modern practice.

interpretation.label: Score 1-2
interpretation.detail: Approximate 1-year mortality ~ 26% in the original cohort.

interpretation.label: Score 3-4
interpretation.detail: Approximate 1-year mortality ~ 52% in the original cohort.

interpretation.label: Score ≥ 5
interpretation.detail: Approximate 1-year mortality ~ 85% in the original cohort — substantial comorbidity burden.

buildNote: The '1-point conditions' and '2-point conditions' items are deliberately implemented as a COUNT-of-how-many-apply select (full range: 0-10 for the 1-point tier, 0-6 for the 2-point tier) rather than 16 individual yes/no toggles, to keep the item list manageable — this reproduces the correct total score identically to itemizing each condition separately, since every condition within a tier is worth the same points, and the option range was deliberately sized to the ACTUAL number of listed conditions per tier (not an arbitrarily truncated '5 or more' bucket, which would have undercounted a patient with unusually high comorbidity burden). The condition list itself is stated in full in each item's label. Mortality percentages are the original 1987 cohort's figures, reproduced as commonly cited — flagged as order-of-magnitude, not a modern precise estimate, the same caveat applied to timi-stemi's mortality table in Batch 3.
